audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL and CL logic: CL fork transitions (Altair), CL validator attestation/proposal/slashing protection (Phase 0), CL light client sync protocol, EL precompiles (MODEXP, BN128), EL networking (eth/70 paginated receipts), and DApp/provider interfaces (EIP-1901, EIP-2696, EIP-2844).

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, crafted precompile inputs for DoS (MODEXP/BN128 gas exhaustion), exploit provider trust model
Send invalid/incomplete paginated receipt data, eclipse attacks, memory exhaustion via unbounded pagination

cl_vectors.threat: Propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, exploit fork transition edge cases
Serve stale/forged bootstrap data, withhold updates, eclipse light clients
Trick validator into double-signing via malicious signing requests, far-future attestation attacks

misclassified_entities.reason: Not an external entity but a label for raw call data within the EVM execution context. The actual external entity is the contract caller.
Threat actor description, not a concrete external entity with a defined protocol entry point. Third-party scripts share the same browser JS context as DApps.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/DApp via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public, unauthenticated interface. Any user or DApp can submit arbitrary requests. Covers EXT-RPC-CLIENT, EXT-RPC-CALLER, EXT-DAPP, EXT-DAPP-CLIENT from source subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL/STATICCALL/DELEGATECALL to precompiles (0x05 MODEXP, 0x06-0x08 BN128)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any smart contract can invoke precompiles with arbitrary input. No authentication. Covers EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT, EXT-ZK-VERIFIER from source subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via eth/70 P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Can send malformed, incomplete, or malicious receipt data. Covers EXT-PEER-NODE, EXT-REQUESTING-PEER from source subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Extension via Browser Injection
trusted_external_entities.rationale: While user-installed, the wallet extension injects code into the browser context. A compromised or malicious extension could intercept/modify all provider interactions. Trust is implicit, not verified.

trusted_external_entities.name: End User via Wallet UI
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Wallet approval/rejection prompts (transaction signing, DID auth consent)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users may be social-engineered into approving malicious transactions. User consent is a trust boundary but not a guarantee of correctness.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum Node via JSON-RPC Backend
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC responses from remote node to provider
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApp-connected nodes may be untrusted third-party services. Response data must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Node via Validator Client API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Validator Client API (signing requests, duty assignments, chain state)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validator client MUST treat the beacon node as potentially compromised. Signing requests must be checked against slashing protection DB. Covers EXT-BEACON-NODE, EXT-BEACON-NODE-UNTRUSTED.

trusted_external_entities.name: CL P2P Gossip Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers are unauthenticated. Attestations and aggregates from gossip must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: ETH1 Chain via Deposit Contract
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: ETH1 deposit data and block hashes for ETH1 voting
trusted_external_entities.rationale: ETH1 data is sourced from an external chain. Merkle proofs for deposits must be verified. A compromised ETH1 endpoint could feed invalid deposit data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client via LC Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light clients request data from full nodes. From the full node's perspective, serving light clients is a resource expenditure; requests must be rate-limited. From the light client's perspective, all data from full nodes must be verified via Merkle proofs and sync committee signatures.

trusted_external_entities.name: Genesis Config Server via HTTPS
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: HTTP(S) fetch of genesis.json from yolonet.xyz
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External web server. No authentication or integrity verification specified. Compromised server could feed malicious genesis config.

trusted_external_entities.name: EF Bootnode via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p enode connection for peer discovery
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Single bootnode is a centralization risk. P2P connections are unauthenticated beyond node ID.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethstats Server via Reporting Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External monitoring service. Node sends data to it; compromised service could be used for fingerprinting or information disclosure.

trusted_external_entities.name: Protocol Developer via Testnet RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Contract deployment and experimental opcode invocation via testnet RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Developers on ephemeral testnet submit experimental contract bytecode. No authentication; testnet is permissionless.

trusted_external_entities.name: Node Operator via CLI/Config
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Client startup configuration and genesis loading
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Operator initiates node bootstrap. While typically trusted, the trust model should not assume operator always provides correct configuration.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Method must not leak sensitive internal information. Rate limiting recommended to prevent enumeration abuse.
All RPC method calls must be validated. Reserved rpc.* namespace must be enforced.
Provider must validate RequestArguments. Sensitive methods must require user authorization (error 4100). Request/response translation must not introduce injection.
Nonce must be verified for freshness/replay protection. Path permissions must be validated. User consent must be obtained before granting permissions.

All length fields and operands must be parsed safely with zero-padding for short inputs. Gas cost must accurately reflect computational complexity to prevent DoS. Modulus-zero edge case must return zero.
Input points must be validated on curve. Coordinates must be checked against field modulus. Invalid inputs must raise OutOfGasError.
G1 point must be validated on curve. Scalar input is arbitrary 256-bit value. Gas cost (6000) must accurately reflect worst-case computation.

Input length must be divisible by 192. All G1/G2 points must be validated on curve AND in correct prime-order subgroup. Gas cost is linear in pair count. Subgroup check is critical for pairing security.

Receipt count must match transaction count. Individual receipt size bounded by gas_limit/8. Total size bounded by block gas limit. Peer must be penalized for invalid data. Buffer sizes must be bounded to prevent memory exhaustion.
Request parameters must be validated. Response size must be bounded. firstBlockReceiptIndex must be within valid range.
DApp must verify provider identity. Multiple provider conflicts must be handled. Injected provider must not be modifiable by page scripts.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Wallet consent UI (transaction signing, DID auth)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: User must be shown clear, accurate information about what they are approving. Phishing-resistant UI required.
Provider should validate response format. Connection should be over secure transport. Timeouts must be implemented.

ALL signing requests MUST be checked against persistent slashing protection DB BEFORE signing. Block proposals must not duplicate slots. Attestations must not create double/surround votes. Far-future attestation check required (~6 hours threshold).

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Validator duty assignment and chain state API
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Committee assignments and chain state from beacon node must be used carefully. Validator should cross-check critical data where possible.
All received attestations must be fully validated (signature, committee membership, slot timing). Invalid attestations must be rejected.
Aggregate proofs must verify selection proof, aggregator index, and aggregate signature. Must be rate-limited.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: ETH1 deposit data and block hash voting
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Deposits must include valid Merkle proofs. ETH1 block candidates must satisfy follow distance and timestamp range. ETH1 endpoint could be compromised.

Full nodes must serve data with valid Merkle proofs. Light clients must verify sync committee signatures and proofs. Updates must be ranked by is_better_update. Data withholding cannot be detected cryptographically.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Genesis configuration loader (HTTP fetch from yolonet.xyz)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Genesis data integrity must be verified (e.g., hash comparison). No authentication specified; HTTPS assumed but not guaranteed.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: devp2p bootnode connection and peer discovery
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Single bootnode is a centralization/availability risk. Peer list from bootnode must not be blindly trusted. Eclipse attack mitigation needed.
Stats data should not leak sensitive node information. Connection should be optional and authenticated.
Experimental opcodes (EIP-2315 subroutines, EIP-2537 BLS) must be fully validated. Standard transaction validation applies.
Configuration inputs should be validated. Genesis file integrity should be verified against known hash.
